WEDNESDAY MYSTERY SOLVED - it is dance season, not a permanent weekly pattern. Over the full 571-day record Wed looked like a standing +1.66 kWh outlier, but splitting the record by period shows the effect exists ONLY between 2026-01-08 and 2026-05-28 (+5.24 kWh vs Tue/Thu); in the other three periods it is -0.72, -0.13 and +0.33, i.e. nothing. Within that window the MEDIAN gap (+6.09) exceeds the mean gap, so it is every Wednesday, not a few outliers, and outdoor temps match (46.4F vs 44.5F) so it is not weather. The excess is concentrated 3-7 PM, peaking 4-5 PM at +1.4 kWh/hr. CONFIRMATION: Monday is also a dance day and shows the same 3-7PM bump in the same window (Mon 8.23, Wed 10.72 vs Tue 6.67, Thu 6.92); outside the window the Mon+Wed vs Tue+Thu gap is -0.08 kWh, i.e. the effect vanishes entirely. So dance days cost MORE despite the family being out in the evening - the spend is in the pre-dance getting-ready block (laundry, early dinner, showers). Magnitude ~2.7 kWh/dance-day, about $20 per season. Lesson for future analysis: averaging day-of-week over the whole record manufactured a phantom year-round pattern out of a 5-month seasonal one. Always split by period before believing a weekday effect.

OIL HEATER MEASURED (middle daughter's bedroom, started 10/19). Overnight 11pm-6am usage stepped from 4.54 kWh/night (10/05-10/18) to 6.92 kWh/night (10/19-10/24) = +2.38 kWh/night, about 340W average over 7h, $0.45/night or roughly $13/month. Daytime usage went DOWN 2.94 kWh over the same split because the warm days of 10/13-10/16 (67-69F) had AC running; that drop is AC ending, not related to the heater.

CALIBRATION EVENT #4 - DRYER ONLY, REPLICATE. 2026-10-27 ~5:32 PM, drying the load washed at 1:49 PM. This is a near-exact repeat of event #2 (10/26 5:38 PM, dryer only) - six minutes apart on consecutive days, same appliance, same configuration, same time-of-day background. WHY THIS MATTERS MOST: a replicate is the only way to estimate MEASUREMENT NOISE. Comparing these two runs tells me how much a dryer figure varies when nothing has actually changed, which sets the error bar on every appliance number in the inventory. Without it I can produce a figure but cannot say whether a difference of, say, 0.4 kWh between two runs is a real effect or just scatter. FULL SET NOW: (1) 10/26 12:40PM washer+dryer, (2) 10/26 5:38PM dryer, (3) 10/27 1:49PM washer, (4) 10/27 5:32PM dryer. Gives direct measurement of each appliance, an additivity check (2+3 vs 1), and a repeatability check (2 vs 4). Load size/wetness will differ between dryer runs - #4 followed a normal wash, #2 followed the 12:40 wash - so some spread between them is genuine variation in the load, not instrument error. Treat the 2-vs-4 gap as an UPPER bound on noise, not a pure one.
